prose_updates.tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, graph dependence, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit benchmark has lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. The finite-sample bridge bounds the difference from Li and Wager's finite indirect effect by the displayed degree-exact smoothness and isolate terms, and this difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\) along maintained sequences in the stated sparsity regime. Li and Wager's equation~(43) is transferred only on the intersection with every source hypothesis and under \(\liminf_n\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\); no containment of the maintained class in their theorem is asserted. Because same-class testing gives only \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) for isolates while the safe interval pays \(B\pi_{0,n}\), no sharp minimax or honest expected-length frontier is claimed, and a rate-sharp feasible PC construction at logarithmic degree remains open.
prose_updates.related_work: LiWager2022RandomGraph is the central asymptotic comparator. Its Proposition~1 and equations~(4)--(5) relate its finite indirect effect to an average derivative through a minimum-degree remainder, while its Theorem~6 and equation~(43) give \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\)-scale Gaussian limits under the full source conditions recorded in \({\rm lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\). The present target \(\theta_n\) is the distinct realized finite-population midpoint derivative. Proposition~\({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) proves a degree-exact conditional comparison retaining isolates and proves that the center difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\) in the stated maintained-class sparsity regime. Transfer of equation~(43) is made only after intersecting with every source hypothesis and imposing \(\liminf_n\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\); it is neither a finite-sample equality nor a claim that the maintained class satisfies Li and Wager's theorem. HuLiWager2022AverageDirectIndirect supplies the Bernoulli-policy decomposition and causal interpretation. ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest informs the computable smoothness-bias interval geometry, while CaiLow2004Adaptation informs the testing-to-expected-length argument; neither treats network support or spectral residualization. AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise and TangCape2025InfiniteRank inform empirical-eigenspace analysis but do not control the exact-support causal score. Leung2022NetworkInference concerns locality-based inference for level effects. BhadraSchweinberger2025Survey is used only as a broad survey of network-interference frameworks.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) is the target and is not defined to equal Li and Wager's finite indirect effect. Proposition~\({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) gives their conditional degree-exact separation, including isolates, and proves an \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\) center approximation along maintained sequences with fixed \(B\) and \(\kappa\) in the stated sparsity regime. LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem~6 is used only on the further intersection with all of its source hypotheses, with treatment probability one half and \(\liminf_n\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\); there is no theorem-wide transfer to every law in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) and no transfer to a distinct target. Every positive realized degree is handled by its exact support radius, and isolates remain visible in the certificate. The supported-unit lattice, interior, and graph-floor terms have a lower benchmark, while the conservative feasible envelope is presented only as an upper side of a bracket. A full matched frontier is not claimed because the safe \(B\pi_{0,n}\) isolate allowance is not matched by the \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) isolate testing term. A rate-sharp feasible PC construction at logarithmic degree, unknown rank, unknown \(L\), simultaneous policy bands, and optimal ego-cluster design remain outside the proved scope.
